question: Which section of BNS 2023 deals with voluntarily throwing or attempting to throw acid (corresponding to Section 326B IPC)?
options: Section 124(2)
Section 125
Section 126
Section 128
explanation: Section 124(2) BNS covers throwing or attempting to throw acid, punishable with imprisonment of not less than 5 years up to 7 years.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; BNS Section 124(2) corresponds to IPC Section 326B.
optionBreakdown.B: Section 125 covers act endangering life or personal safety.
optionBreakdown.D: Section 128 covers causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons.

learningObjective: Identify BNS section for attempt to throw acid.

question: What is the statutory punishment for Voluntarily Causing Hurt under Section 115(2) BNS (Section 323 IPC)?
options: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs 10,000, or both, or community service
Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine
Rigorous imprisonment for 6 months only
Fine of Rs 500 only
explanation: Section 115(2) BNS punishes voluntarily causing hurt with imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs 10,000, or both, or with community service.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; includes community service in BNS.
optionBreakdown.B: Incorrect period.
optionBreakdown.D: Old IPC fine was Rs 1,000; BNS increases fine and adds community service.

learningObjective: Recall updated penalties for simple hurt under BNS.

question: What did the Supreme Court hold in Laxmi v. Union of India (2014) regarding acid attack victims?
options: Regulation of acid sales, minimum compensation of Rs 3 lakhs, and free medical treatment in all hospitals
Complete ban on industrial use of acids
Trial of acid attacks only by military tribunals
Victim must bear 50% of reconstructive surgery costs
explanation: Laxmi v. Union of India ((2014) 4 SCC 427) mandated retail acid regulation, mandatory minimum compensation, and free medical treatment under CrPC S. 357C / BNSS S. 397.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; seminal Laxmi judgment directives.
optionBreakdown.B: Industrial sales are regulated, not completely banned.
optionBreakdown.C: Tried by Sessions Court, not military tribunals.

learningObjective: Analyze Laxmi v. UOI acid attack guidelines.

question: If A cuts off B's little finger, which clause of Grievous Hurt does this act fall under?
options: Clause Sixth: Permanent privation of any member or joint
Clause First: Emasculation
Clause Second: Permanent privation of the sight of eye
It is only simple hurt because a little finger is not vital
explanation: Permanent privation of any member or joint (including any finger or toe) is grievous hurt under Clause Sixth.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; finger is a member/joint under Clause Sixth.
optionBreakdown.B: Clause First is emasculation.
optionBreakdown.C: Clause Second is sight of eye.
optionBreakdown.D: Cutting off a finger is explicitly grievous hurt.

provision: BNS S. 116 Clause 6 / IPC S. 320 Clause 6
learningObjective: Apply Grievous Hurt clauses to factual scenarios.

question: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means is punished under:
options: Section 117 BNS (Section 324 IPC)
Section 118(1) BNS (Section 324 IPC)
Section 120 BNS
Section 130 BNS
explanation: Section 118(1) BNS corresponds to Section 324 IPC (voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means, up to 3 years imprisonment or fine).

optionBreakdown.A: Section 117 covers Voluntarily causing grievous hurt.
optionBreakdown.B: Correct; Section 118(1) covers hurt by dangerous weapons.

learningObjective: Map dangerous weapons hurt provisions.

question: Wrongful Restraint under Section 126(1) BNS (Section 339 IPC) is defined as:
options: Voluntarily obstructing any person so as to prevent that person from proceeding in any direction in which that person has a right to proceed
Restraining a person within circumscribed limits
Restraining a person inside a locked room
Tying a person with ropes
explanation: Wrongful restraint is partial restraint preventing movement in a particular direction where the person has a legal right to proceed.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; statutory definition of wrongful restraint.
optionBreakdown.B: Restraint within circumscribed limits is wrongful confinement.
optionBreakdown.D: Method is irrelevant; direction is the defining test.

learningObjective: Define wrongful restraint.

question: Wrongful Confinement under Section 127(1) BNS (Section 340 IPC) requires:
options: Restraining a person in a single direction only
Wrongfully restraining a person in such a manner as to prevent that person from proceeding beyond certain circumscribing limits
Detaining a person for more than 24 hours
Use of physical iron chains
explanation: Wrongful confinement is total restraint in all directions within bounded circumscribing limits.

optionBreakdown.A: Single direction is wrongful restraint.
optionBreakdown.B: Correct; circumscribing limits define wrongful confinement.
optionBreakdown.C: Duration affects punishment under S. 127(3)-(5), but not the core definition.
optionBreakdown.D: Physical chains are not mandatory; psychological or physical walls suffice.

learningObjective: Define wrongful confinement.

question: What is the statutory punishment for Wrongful Restraint under Section 126(2) BNS (Section 341 IPC)?
options: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both
Rigorous imprisonment up to 1 year
Imprisonment up to 3 years
Fine of Rs 100 only
explanation: Section 126(2) BNS prescribes simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; up to 1 month simple imprisonment or fine up to Rs 5,000.
optionBreakdown.B: Too severe.
optionBreakdown.D: Old IPC fine was Rs 500; BNS raised it to Rs 5,000.

learningObjective: Recall punishment for wrongful restraint.

question: What is the statutory punishment for general Wrongful Confinement under Section 127(2) BNS (Section 342 IPC)?
options: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both
Simple imprisonment up to 1 month
Rigorous imprisonment up to 5 years
Fine only
explanation: Section 127(2) BNS provides imprisonment of either description up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both.
optionBreakdown.B: 1 month applies to wrongful restraint.
optionBreakdown.C: 5 years applies to confinement for 10 or more days.

learningObjective: Recall punishment for wrongful confinement.

question: Under the Exception to Section 126(1) BNS (Section 339 IPC), which of the following does NOT constitute wrongful restraint?
options: Obstruction of a private way over land or water which a person in good faith believes himself to have a lawful right to obstruct
Obstructing a public highway with bullock carts
Stopping a passenger train illegally
Blocking a hospital gate
explanation: The Exception to S. 126(1) protects bona fide obstruction of a private way over land or water based on good faith belief of lawful right.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; bona fide assertion of private property right is protected.
optionBreakdown.B: Public highway obstruction is wrongful restraint.
optionBreakdown.C: Obstructing train is wrongful restraint and railway offence.

provision: BNS S. 126(1) Exception / IPC S. 339 Exception
learningObjective: Master exception to wrongful restraint.

question: If a person is wrongfully confined for 3 or more days, what is the maximum punishment under Section 127(3) BNS (Section 343 IPC)?
options: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
Imprisonment up to 5 years
Life imprisonment
explanation: Confinement for 3 days or more is punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both under S. 127(3) BNS / S. 343 IPC.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; up to 2 years for 3 or more days.
optionBreakdown.B: 3 years applies to 10 or more days.

learningObjective: Differentiate confinement durations and penalties.

question: If a person is wrongfully confined for 10 or more days, what is the maximum punishment under Section 127(4) BNS (Section 344 IPC)?
options: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine
Imprisonment up to 5 years
Imprisonment up to 7 years
Imprisonment up to 10 years
explanation: Confinement for 10 days or more is punishable with imprisonment of either description up to 3 years, and fine (S. 127(4) BNS / S. 344 IPC).

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; up to 3 years and fine.
optionBreakdown.B: Incorrect.

learningObjective: Identify penalty for 10+ days wrongful confinement.

question: A locks the only exit door of a room from outside while Z is sleeping inside. What offence has A committed?
options: Wrongful Confinement
Wrongful Restraint only
Attempt to Murder
No offence until Z wakes up and tries to exit
explanation: Locking a person inside a room sets total circumscribed limits on their freedom of movement, constituting wrongful confinement.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; locking someone in a room is wrongful confinement.
optionBreakdown.B: Restraint is partial; this is total confinement.
optionBreakdown.D: Confinement is complete upon imposing the circumscribing boundary.

learningObjective: Apply confinement to locked room scenario.

question: What is the key conceptual difference between Wrongful Restraint and Wrongful Confinement?
options: Restraint is partial (in one direction); Confinement is total (in all directions within limits)
Restraint applies to property; Confinement applies to person
Restraint is cognizable; Confinement is non-cognizable
Restraint requires physical force; Confinement requires verbal threats
explanation: Wrongful restraint abridges liberty in a particular direction; wrongful confinement abridges liberty in all directions (Bird v. Jones doctrine).

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; classic partial vs total liberty distinction.
optionBreakdown.B: Both apply to the human person.
optionBreakdown.D: Both can be committed by force or threat.

learningObjective: Distinguish restraint from confinement.

question: Wrongful confinement to extort property or constrain to an illegal act under S. 127(6) BNS (S. 347 IPC) is punishable with:
options: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine
Imprisonment up to 5 years
Rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years
Imprisonment for 6 months only
explanation: Section 127(6) BNS (IPC S. 347) provides imprisonment of either description up to 3 years, and fine.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; up to 3 years and fine.
optionBreakdown.B: Incorrect.

learningObjective: Recall extortion-linked confinement penalty.

question: Under Section 137(1) BNS (Section 359 IPC), Kidnapping is of how many kinds?
options: Two kinds: Kidnapping from India and Kidnapping from lawful guardianship
Three kinds: from India, from state, and from home
Four kinds including international kidnapping
Only one kind
explanation: Section 137(1) BNS (Section 359 IPC) classifies kidnapping into two kinds: (i) from India, and (ii) from lawful guardianship.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; exactly two kinds of kidnapping exist.
optionBreakdown.B: Incorrect.

learningObjective: Recall two kinds of kidnapping.

question: Under Section 137(2) BNS (Section 361 IPC), what are the age limits for kidnapping from lawful guardianship?
options: Male under 16 years, female under 18 years
Male under 18 years, female under 18 years
Any child under 14 years
Under 21 years for both
explanation: Under Section 137(2) BNS (Section 361 IPC), the age limits are a male under 16 years, or a female under 18 years, or any person of unsound mind.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; male under 16, female under 18.
optionBreakdown.B: Equal 18 threshold was proposed but 16/18 is retained in statute.
optionBreakdown.C: 14 is POCSO age in certain contexts, not S. 137(2).

learningObjective: Verify statutory age limits for kidnapping.

question: How is 'Abduction' defined under Section 138 BNS (Section 362 IPC)?
options: Whoever by force compels, or by any deceitful means induces, any person to go from any place
Taking or enticing away a minor from lawful guardian
Conveying any person beyond the limits of India without consent
Trafficking a person across state borders
explanation: Abduction requires compelling by force or inducing by deceitful means any person to go from any place.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; statutory definition of abduction.
optionBreakdown.B: This is kidnapping from lawful guardianship.

learningObjective: Define abduction.

question: Is Abduction per se an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita or Indian Penal Code?
options: Yes, it is punishable with 7 years imprisonment by itself
No; abduction is an auxiliary act and becomes punishable only when accompanied by a specific criminal intent
Yes, it is a non-bailable standalone offence
No, it is only a civil tort
explanation: Abduction per se is not an offence; it becomes punishable only when accompanied by intent to murder (S. 139), wrongfully confine (S. 140), compel marriage, etc.

optionBreakdown.A: Incorrect; abduction alone without purpose is not punishable.
optionBreakdown.B: Correct; abduction is an auxiliary/inchoate element requiring specific statutory purpose.

learningObjective: Master auxiliary nature of abduction.

question: What is the landmark Supreme Court decision on kidnapping where the minor girl left her father's house voluntarily and met the accused on the road?
options: S. Varadarajan v. State of Madras (1965)
State of Haryana v. Rajinder Singh (1996)
Parkash v. State of Haryana (2004)
Kalyani v. State (2012)
explanation: S. Varadarajan v. State of Madras (AIR 1965 SC 942) held that where a minor capable of thinking leaves voluntarily and asks the accused to come, there is no 'taking' or 'enticing'.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; Varadarajan is the leading authority on 'taking or enticing'.
optionBreakdown.B: Deals with dowry death.

learningObjective: Apply S. Varadarajan precedent on kidnapping.

question: Under Section 143 BNS (Section 370 IPC), Human Trafficking includes recruitment, transportation, harboring or receipt of persons by means of:
options: Threat, force, coercion, abduction, fraud, or abuse of power for exploitation
Lawful contractual recruitment through licensed agents
Voluntary domestic migration for employment
Adoption through official CARA channels
explanation: Section 143 BNS (Section 370 IPC) incorporates the UN Palermo Protocol definition of trafficking for physical, sexual, or organ exploitation.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; comprehensive trafficking definition.
optionBreakdown.B: Lawful employment is not trafficking.

learningObjective: Understand human trafficking ingredients.

question: What is the statutory punishment for trafficking more than one person under Section 143(3) BNS (Section 370(3) IPC)?
options: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 10 years, which may extend to life imprisonment, and fine
Imprisonment up to 7 years
Imprisonment for 5 years
Capital punishment
explanation: Trafficking of multiple persons is punishable with rigorous imprisonment of not less than 10 years extending to life imprisonment, and fine.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; minimum 10 years to life.
optionBreakdown.B: 7-10 years applies to single person trafficking.
optionBreakdown.D: Death penalty does not apply to Section 143(3).

learningObjective: Recall penalties for multi-person trafficking.

question: Which section of BNS 2023 deals with Kidnapping for Ransom (corresponding to Section 364A IPC)?
options: Section 140(2)
Section 140(1)
Section 142
Section 144
explanation: Section 140(2) BNS covers kidnapping or abducting for ransom, punishable with death or imprisonment for life, and fine (IPC Section 364A).

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; BNS Section 140(2) corresponds to IPC Section 364A.
optionBreakdown.B: Section 140(1) covers kidnapping with intent to secretly confine.

learningObjective: Identify BNS section for kidnapping for ransom.

question: Can a father be guilty of kidnapping his own legitimate minor child from the custody of the mother under Section 137(2) BNS?
options: Yes, always
No, generally a father is the natural guardian, unless a competent civil court has granted exclusive custody to the mother
Yes, father has no guardianship rights in criminal law
Only if the child is a daughter
explanation: Under Exception to S. 137(2) BNS / S. 361 IPC, a person who in good faith believes himself to be entitled to custody is not guilty, and father is natural guardian unless deprived by court order.

optionBreakdown.A: Incorrect.
optionBreakdown.B: Correct; father as natural guardian is protected unless court stripped custody.

provision: BNS S. 137(2) Exception / IPC S. 361 Exception
learningObjective: Analyze parental custody and kidnapping exception.

question: What is the difference between Kidnapping and Abduction regarding the consent of the victim?
options: Consent of minor in kidnapping is entirely immaterial; in abduction, free and voluntary consent of person removes the offence
Consent is valid in both
Consent is immaterial in both
Minor's consent is valid in kidnapping if above 12 years
explanation: In kidnapping from guardianship, consent of the minor is completely irrelevant (consent must be of guardian); in abduction, free consent negates force/deceit.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; consent of minor is immaterial in kidnapping.
optionBreakdown.B: Incorrect.

learningObjective: Compare consent in kidnapping vs abduction.

question: Under Section 63 BNS (Section 375 IPC), what is the statutory age threshold below which sexual intercourse with a female is rape regardless of her consent?
options: Under 16 years
Under 18 years
Under 21 years
Under 15 years
explanation: Under Clause Sixth of Section 63 BNS (and Section 375 IPC), sexual intercourse with a female under 18 years of age is rape with or without her consent.

optionBreakdown.A: Old pre-2013 age limit was 16; Criminal Law Amendment 2013 raised it to 18.
optionBreakdown.B: Correct; under 18 years is the statutory threshold.

provision: BNS S. 63 Clause 6 / IPC S. 375 Clause 6
learningObjective: Verify statutory age threshold in rape.

question: What is the minimum statutory punishment for simple Rape under Section 64(1) BNS (Section 376(1) IPC)?
options: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 7 years
Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 10 years, which may extend to life, and fine
Imprisonment up to 5 years
Rigorous imprisonment for 3 years
explanation: Section 64(1) BNS prescribes rigorous imprisonment of not less than 10 years extending to life imprisonment, and fine.

optionBreakdown.A: 7 years was the old pre-2018 minimum.
optionBreakdown.B: Correct; 10 years minimum under BNS S. 64(1) and post-2018 IPC S. 376(1).

learningObjective: Recall minimum sentence for rape.

question: What is the punishment for Gang Rape under Section 70(1) BNS (Section 376D IPC)?
options: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years, which may extend to life (natural life), and fine
Imprisonment for 10 years
Imprisonment up to 14 years
Simple imprisonment for 7 years
explanation: Section 70(1) BNS (IPC S. 376D) punishes gang rape with rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years, extending to life (remainder of natural life), and fine.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; minimum 20 years extending to natural life.
optionBreakdown.B: Incorrect.

learningObjective: Recall gang rape statutory penalty.

question: Under Section 70(2) BNS (Section 376DA IPC), what is the punishment for gang rape of a woman under 18 years of age?
options: Imprisonment for life (natural life) and fine, or death
Imprisonment for 10 years only
Rigorous imprisonment for 7 years
Fine of Rs 1 lakh only
explanation: Section 70(2) BNS provides imprisonment for the remainder of natural life and fine, or death.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; natural life or death.
optionBreakdown.B: Too lenient.

learningObjective: Master aggravated child gang rape penalties.

question: How is 'Consent' defined in Explanation 2 to Section 63 BNS (Section 375 IPC)?
options: An unequivocal voluntary agreement when the woman by words, gestures or any form of verbal or non-verbal communication, communicates willingness
Passive submission without physical resistance
Absence of physical injuries on the body of the woman
Consent inferred from previous sexual history
explanation: Consent is defined as an unequivocal voluntary agreement by words, gestures or non-verbal communication. Lack of physical resistance does not imply consent.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; statutory definition of consent in Explanation 2.
optionBreakdown.B: Proviso explicitly states lack of physical resistance does not constitute consent.
optionBreakdown.C: Absence of injuries does not imply consent.
optionBreakdown.D: Previous sexual history is inadmissible under S. 53A IEA / S. 53 BSA.

provision: BNS S. 63 Expl 2 / IPC S. 375 Expl 2
learningObjective: Understand affirmative consent definition.

question: Which landmark case led to the appointment of the Justice Verma Committee and subsequent radical overhaul of sexual offences in Indian criminal law?
options: Mukesh & Anr. v. State for NCT of Delhi (2017) (Nirbhaya Case)
Tukaram v. State of Maharashtra (1979) (Mathura Case)
Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)
Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017)
explanation: The 2012 Delhi gang rape (Nirbhaya case) prompted the Verma Committee recommendations leading to Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; Nirbhaya case catalyzed the modern rape law reform.
optionBreakdown.B: Mathura case led to 1983 amendment introducing custodial rape provisions.
optionBreakdown.C: Vishaka deals with workplace sexual harassment guidelines.
optionBreakdown.D: Independent Thought removed marital rape exception for wives aged 15-18.

learningObjective: Contextualize rape law reforms.

question: In Independent Thought v. Union of India ((2017) 10 SCC 800), what did the Supreme Court hold regarding Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC (now Exception 2 to S. 63 BNS)?
options: Sexual intercourse by a man with his wife, who is not under 18 years, is not rape; marital exception for girls between 15-18 was struck down
Marital rape exception was declared entirely unconstitutional for all ages
Child marriage was declared void ab initio under criminal law
Age of consent was reduced to 16 years
explanation: Independent Thought held that Exception 2 protecting sex with a child wife aged 15-18 violated Article 14, 15, 21, and read it down so that intercourse with any wife under 18 is rape.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; struck down exception for child wives under 18.
optionBreakdown.B: General marital rape for adult wives over 18 was not decided in this judgment.
optionBreakdown.C: Dealt with penal law exception, not civil validity.

learningObjective: Master Independent Thought child wife precedent.

question: What is the statutory punishment under Section 66 BNS (Section 376A IPC) for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim in rape?
options: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years extending to life (natural life), or with death
Imprisonment for 10 years
Imprisonment up to 14 years
Life imprisonment with remission after 10 years
explanation: Section 66 BNS provides rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years up to natural life, or with death.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; 20 years to natural life, or death.
optionBreakdown.B: Too lenient.
optionBreakdown.D: No remission applies where natural life is specified.

learningObjective: Recall penalties for vegetative state/death in rape.

question: Under Section 64(2) BNS (Section 376(2) IPC), aggravated forms of rape include rape committed by:
options: Police officer, public servant, member of armed forces, or hospital/jail management on person in their custody
Any stranger on a highway
A co-worker in a private office
Any person during night hours
explanation: Section 64(2) BNS enumerates aggravated rape including custodial rape by police, public servants, armed forces, jail/hospital superintendents.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; custodial and fiduciary positions constitute aggravated rape.
optionBreakdown.B: Not per se an aggravated category under S. 64(2).
optionBreakdown.C: Covered under workplace harassment or general rape.

learningObjective: Identify aggravated custodial rape categories.

question: What is the punishment for rape of a woman under 16 years of age under Section 65(1) BNS (Section 376DA / 376(3) IPC)?
options: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years which may extend to life (natural life), and fine
Imprisonment for 7 years
Imprisonment up to 10 years
Simple imprisonment for 5 years
explanation: Section 65(1) BNS prescribes rigorous imprisonment of not less than 20 years extending to remainder of natural life, and fine.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; minimum 20 years up to natural life.
optionBreakdown.B: Too low.

learningObjective: Recall penalties for rape of girl under 16.

question: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty is punishable under:
options: Section 74 BNS (Section 354 IPC)
Section 75 BNS (Section 354A IPC)
Section 77 BNS (Section 354C IPC)
Section 78 BNS (Section 354D IPC)
explanation: Section 74 BNS corresponds to Section 354 IPC (assault or criminal force with intent to outrage modesty, 1 to 5 years and fine).

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; BNS Section 74 corresponds to IPC Section 354.
optionBreakdown.B: Section 75 is Sexual Harassment (S. 354A IPC).

learningObjective: Map section for outraging modesty.

question: In State of Punjab v. Major Singh (AIR 1967 SC 63), what did the Supreme Court hold regarding the 'modesty' of a female child aged seven and a half months?
options: Even a female infant possesses the modesty of a woman from the moment of birth capable of being outraged
An infant does not possess modesty until attaining puberty
Modesty requires sexual consciousness by the victim
Modesty can only be outraged if the child cries
explanation: Major Singh (1967) held that modesty is an attribute of the female sex from birth, and subjective consciousness of the victim is irrelevant.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; Major Singh held modesty attaches to female sex from birth.
optionBreakdown.B: Overruled/rejected by SC.

learningObjective: Master Major Singh doctrine on modesty.

question: Under Section 75 BNS (Section 354A IPC), which of the following acts does NOT constitute the offence of Sexual Harassment?
options: Physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures
A demand or request for sexual favours
Showing pornography against the will of a woman
Politely asking a woman for professional directions on a public road
explanation: Asking professional directions without unwelcome sexual undertones is lawful conduct.

optionBreakdown.A: Constitutes S. 75(1)(i).
optionBreakdown.B: Constitutes S. 75(1)(ii).
optionBreakdown.D: Correct; asking directions is not sexual harassment.

learningObjective: Identify ingredients of sexual harassment.

question: What is the statutory punishment for Voyeurism on a first conviction under Section 77 BNS (Section 354C IPC)?
options: Imprisonment of not less than 1 year up to 3 years, and fine
Imprisonment of not less than 3 years up to 7 years, and fine
Fine of Rs 1,000 only
Life imprisonment
explanation: First conviction for voyeurism carries imprisonment of not less than 1 year extending up to 3 years, and fine (second conviction: 3 to 7 years).

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; 1 to 3 years and fine on first conviction.
optionBreakdown.B: 3 to 7 years applies on second or subsequent conviction.

learningObjective: Recall voyeurism sentencing tiers.

question: Under Section 78 BNS (Section 354D IPC), Stalking includes which of the following conducts?
options: Following a woman and contacting or attempting to contact her repeatedly despite clear disinterest
Monitoring the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication
Both (A) and (B)
Only physical stalking on roads
explanation: Section 78 BNS (IPC S. 354D) penalises both physical following/contacting and cyber-stalking (monitoring internet/email/electronic communication).

optionBreakdown.A: Covers physical stalking.
optionBreakdown.B: Covers cyber stalking.
optionBreakdown.C: Correct; both physical and cyber stalking are covered.

learningObjective: Master physical and cyber stalking.

question: Under Section 76 BNS (Section 354B IPC), assault or use of criminal force to a woman with intent to disrobe is punishable with:
options: Imprisonment of not less than 3 years which may extend to 7 years, and fine
Imprisonment up to 1 year
Fine of Rs 5,000 only
Life imprisonment
explanation: Section 76 BNS prescribes imprisonment of not less than 3 years extending up to 7 years, and fine.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; 3 to 7 years and fine.
optionBreakdown.B: Too lenient.

learningObjective: Recall punishment for intent to disrobe.

question: Which of the following is a statutory exception where conduct does NOT amount to Stalking under Section 78 BNS?
options: Pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime by a person entrusted with that responsibility by the State
Pursued under any law or to comply with any condition imposed under any law
In that particular circumstance, the conduct was reasonable and justified
All of the above
explanation: All three are statutory exceptions under the Proviso to Section 78(1) BNS (Section 354D(1) IPC).

optionBreakdown.A: Statutory exception under clause (a).
optionBreakdown.B: Statutory exception under clause (b).
optionBreakdown.D: Correct; all three are recognised defences to stalking.

provision: BNS S. 78 Proviso / IPC S. 354D Proviso
learningObjective: Master statutory defences to stalking.

question: In Rupan Deol Bajaj v. K.P.S. Gill ((1995) 6 SCC 194), slapping a woman on her posterior at a dinner party was held to constitute:
options: Outraging modesty under Section 354 IPC (now BNS S. 74) and insult under Section 509 IPC (now BNS S. 79)
Only simple assault under Section 352 IPC
No offence because it occurred in a private social gathering
A non-cognizable civil tort only
explanation: Rupan Deol Bajaj established that slapping or touching private parts with sexual undertone outrages modesty under S. 354 and S. 509 regardless of social status.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; convicted under S. 354 and S. 509.
optionBreakdown.B: Not reduced to simple assault.
optionBreakdown.C: Venue does not immunize the offence.
optionBreakdown.D: Held to be a serious penal offence.

learningObjective: Analyze Rupan Deol Bajaj modesty precedent.

question: What is the punishment on a second or subsequent conviction for Stalking under Section 78(2) BNS (Section 354D(2) IPC)?
options: Imprisonment up to 5 years, and fine
Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine
Imprisonment up to 10 years
Life imprisonment
explanation: First conviction carries up to 3 years and fine; second conviction carries imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; up to 5 years and fine on repeat conviction.
optionBreakdown.B: 3 years is for first conviction.

learningObjective: Recall recidivist stalking penalties.

question: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman under Section 79 BNS (Section 509 IPC) carries what maximum punishment under BNS 2023?
options: Simple imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine
Simple imprisonment up to 1 year only
Fine of Rs 500 only
7 years rigorous imprisonment
explanation: Under BNS Section 79 (IPC S. 509), the punishment is simple imprisonment for a term up to 3 years, and fine (increased from 1 year in earlier law).

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; up to 3 years and fine.
optionBreakdown.B: 1 year was the pre-amendment IPC term.

learningObjective: Recognize enhanced penalty for insulting modesty under BNS.

question: How has BNS 2023 structured the former Section 498A IPC (Cruelty by Husband or Relatives)?
options: Split into Section 85 (Punishment for cruelty: up to 3 years and fine) and Section 86 (Statutory definition of Cruelty)
Abolished entirely
Merged into Section 106
Retained as a non-cognizable civil dispute
explanation: BNS 2023 innovatively bifurcated Section 498A IPC into Section 85 (punishment clause) and Section 86 (substantive definition of cruelty).

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; Section 85 provides penalty and Section 86 provides the definition.
optionBreakdown.B: Not abolished.

learningObjective: Master statutory bifurcation of S. 498A IPC into BNS S. 85 & 86.

question: Under Section 86 BNS, 'Cruelty' means:
options: Any wilful conduct of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to coerce unlawful property demands
Mere incompatibility of temper between spouses
Occasional domestic arguments without harassment
Filing for lawful divorce in family court
explanation: Section 86 BNS defines cruelty under two limbs: (a) wilful conduct driving to suicide or grave injury/danger to life/limb/health; and (b) harassment for unlawful property/security demands.

optionBreakdown.A: Correct; two-pronged statutory definition of cruelty in Section 86.
optionBreakdown.B: Incompatibility is not criminal cruelty.
optionBreakdown.C: Ordinary wear and tear is not cruelty.
optionBreakdown.D: Exercising legal remedy is not cruelty.

learningObjective: Define cruelty under BNS S. 86.

question: Which groundbreaking new provision is introduced in Section 69 BNS 2023?
options: Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means or false promise of marriage
Adultery as a penal offence with 5 years imprisonment
Mandatory pre-nuptial arbitration in all marriages
Criminalisation of live-in relationships
explanation: Section 69 BNS creates a specific standalone offence for sexual intercourse by deceitful means (inducing false promise of employment/promotion or marrying without intention of fulfilling it).
